part_a.one_line: Mixed evidence -- do not stretch it either way. The per-scene VARIATION is not a pure global shift: broadcasting the predicted-mean scale as one constant does NOT reproduce the tall-tail gain (>15 m MAE mean-global 16.9 vs adaptive 9.1). BUT the predictor does not track the true per-scene oracle scale on held-out JAX (Spearman 0.036 << 0.35) and it worsens the OMA building body (5.34->6.11 MAE) -- a crude tall-responsive scale boost, not genuine scene-specific metric calibration.

resize_pipeline.note: load_sample() resizes every raster to (tile_size, tile_size); measured raw dims are square and equal to tile_size, so the resize is a near-no-op and does NOT normalize differing physical resolutions within this pipeline. A true GSD is unavailable (identity ModelTransformation stub, no CRS) so a physical-resolution mismatch between splits cannot be measured from these files and is NOT assumed.

answers.s29_physical_scale: Image-resolution/GSD: No meaningful evidence. Metric depth→height scale: Strong evidence.
questions: A1. Was the predicted adaptive scale actually adapting?
No — held-out JAX scale Spearman 0.036 (needs >=0.35 to claim tracking); OMA Spearman 0.589.
A2. How did it compare with the predicted-mean global scale?
OMA building MAE adaptive 6.11 vs predicted-mean-global 5.34 (Δ 0.78); >15 m MAE adaptive 9.15 vs mean-global 16.91 (Δ -7.76).
A3. Was the tall improvement genuine scene adaptation or a global upward shift?
Mixed / inconclusive — per-scene variation beats its own mean.
A4. What does the evidence say about Experiment #6?

MIXED_INCONCLUSIVE: Mixed evidence -- do not stretch it either way. The per-scene VARIATION is not a pure global shift: broadcasting the predicted-mean scale as one constant does NOT reproduce the tall-tail gain (>15 m MAE mean-global 16.9 vs adaptive 9.1). BUT the predictor does not track the true per-scene oracle scale on held-out JAX (Spearman 0.036 << 0.35) and it worsens the OMA building body (5.34->6.11 MAE) -- a crude tall-responsive scale boost, not genuine scene-specific metric calibration.
B5. Do JAX train, JAX val and OMA have different physical/image scales?

Image-resolution/GSD: No meaningful evidence (GSD unavailable in this mirror; RGB tile shapes identical across splits). Metric depth→height scale: Strong evidence (oracle slope JAX mean 7.72 vs OMA 2.91, ratio 2.65×, Cohen's d 1.14).
B6. Do their Depth Anything distributions differ?
Weak evidence — train↔OMA histogram overlap 0.862 (1.0 = identical); depth median JAX 1.288 vs OMA 1.442.
B7. Do their height distributions differ?
Moderate evidence — median building height JAX 5.9 m vs OMA 4.3 m; >15 m building fraction JAX 0.210 vs OMA 0.111; >30 m JAX 0.071 vs OMA 0.052.
B8. Do their oracle depth→height slopes differ?
Strong evidence — the single most important diagnostic: JAX slope median 7.07 vs OMA 2.46, KS 0.53.
B9. Does OMA contain different/taller structure exposure?
OMA >15 m building fraction 0.111 vs JAX 0.210 (ratio 0.53×); OMA max building height 44.3 m vs JAX 186.5 m.
B10. Are large/tall structures represented sufficiently in JAX training?
Strong evidence that training is representative — 39/102 train tiles have >20 m buildings (0.38), 14 have >30 m (0.14); OMA oracle scale median inside the JAX P5–P95 slope range [1.13, 13.87].
B11. Is there evidence of GSD/resolution mismatch?

No meaningful evidence — a physical GSD is not present in the mirror files (identity ModelTransformation stub, no CRS/GeoKeyDirectory) so it cannot be measured and is not invented; RGB tile shapes are identical across splits.
B12. Is there evidence of crop/tile/structure-size mismatch?
Weak evidence — mean largest building component JAX 20696 px vs OMA 15780 px (ratio 0.76×); tall-building edge-touch fraction JAX 0.18 vs OMA 0.12.
B13. Is there evidence of label preprocessing inconsistency?
No meaningful evidence — JAX/OMA both ground-floored (min 0.00/0.00 m), no negatives (frac 0.0000/0.0000); preprocessing appears consistent across cities.
B14. Which explanation has the strongest evidence?

Combination, dominated by a cross-city depth→metric-height SCALE shift plus geographic/domain shift — NOT an image-GSD/resolution difference (unmeasurable here, tiles identical) and NOT missing metric information (the Exp-5 per-image oracle recovers tall height, so the signal is present). Oracle-slope shift: Strong evidence; DA-V2 depth-distribution shift: Weak evidence. Training-data tall-structure imbalance is a secondary contributor. Part A shows Exp-6's predicted per-scene scale does not track the true scale on held-out JAX (so it is not reliably image-inferable), even though its variation crudely helps the OMA tall tail — consistent with the shift being domain-driven rather than image-recoverable.
B15. Single strongest next experimental direction?

k-SHOT TARGET-CITY SCALE CALIBRATION (probe, DO NOT EXECUTE here): re-fit the SAME per-scene oracle depth→height relationship using only k∈{1,2,4,8} labelled OMA scenes as anchors, and measure how quickly the OMA building/tall MAE approaches the oracle. Rationale: (i) Part A shows the predicted per-scene scale does not track held-out in-domain scale (not reliably image-inferable) and a single mean scale does not reproduce the tall-tail gain; (ii) Part B shows a strong, systematic JAX→OMA oracle-slope shift; (iii) Exp-5 shows the per-scene oracle DOES recover tall height. Together these say the missing ingredient is a little in-domain metric anchoring, not a new loss/architecture/receptive-field. A GSD/metadata probe is NOT actionable on this mirror (no GSD present). This is a domain-adaptation measurement, still no production/DSM/3D.
